cards.title: Scaled dot-product attention
cards.problem: Token vectors at [B,T,D] do not interact; each position is isolated until something mixes context.
cards.mechanism: Q×Kᵀ → scale by √d_k → causal mask → softmax → weighted sum of V. Every token can attend to allowed past keys.
cards.buy: Global, content-based mixing; the core of modern decoders.
cards.give_up: Compute grows ≈ T²; KV memory grows ≈ T per user — both become painful at long context.
cards.when: Default building block whenever you need full causal mixing and can afford quadratic prefill at your target T.

source.label: Vaswani et al. — Attention Is All You Need

cards.title: Absolute learned position embeddings
cards.problem: Attention scores are permutation-invariant; the model cannot tell token order without extra position signal.
cards.mechanism: Add a learned vector per absolute position index to token embeddings before the stack.
cards.buy: Simple to implement; works well up to trained max length.
cards.give_up: Does not extrapolate past trained positions; table size grows with max sequence length.
cards.when: Short, fixed-context models where train and serve lengths match.

source.label: Vaswani et al. — learned PE variant (Transformer §3.5)

cards.sec_note: §8 position prelim (oldest PE) before RoPE major

cards.title: Sinusoidal position encoding
cards.problem: Learned absolute tables tie capacity to max length and can overfit positions seen in training.
cards.mechanism: Fixed sin/cos waves at multiple frequencies encode absolute index; added to embeddings.
cards.buy: No learned position table; smooth relative structure in the encoding itself.
cards.give_up: Still absolute-index based; length extrapolation is not a free lunch for attention beyond train horizon.
cards.when: Teaching and architectures that want deterministic, parameter-free position features.

source.label: Vaswani et al. — sinusoidal PE formulation (§3.5)

cards.sec_note: §8 Vaswani PE cluster; listed after RoPE major in Te_No to keep rope=8

cards.title: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE)
cards.problem: Content-only q·k is distance-blind; causal mask alone does not encode how far apart tokens are.
cards.mechanism: Rotate Q/K pairs by position-dependent angles so dot products depend on relative offset (j−i).
cards.buy: Relative position in the score; strong default in open LLMs.
cards.give_up: Extrapolation past train length needs scaling tricks (NTK/YaRN/DroPE) or native long training.
cards.when: Rotary-friendly stacks at moderate context; pair with extension method for much longer serve lengths.

source.label: Su et al. — RoFormer / Rotary Position Embedding

cards.title: ALiBi (Attention with Linear Biases)
cards.problem: RoPE-family methods still tie position to rotations; some teams want distance penalty without rotary dims.
cards.mechanism: Add linear bias to attention logits based on key-query distance instead of explicit rotary embedding.
cards.buy: Simple distance prior; can help length generalization in some setups.
cards.give_up: Hard-coded distance prior may be wrong for tasks where far tokens matter equally.
cards.when: When you want a lightweight positional inductive bias without full RoPE machinery.

source.label: Press, Smith, Lewis — Train Short, Test Long (ALiBi)

cards.sec_note: Position/bias family; assignment cover; no own h1

cards.title: Multi-Query Attention (MQA)
cards.problem: KV cache bytes scale with H_KV; serving many users makes memory the bottleneck, not just FLOPs.
cards.mechanism: Many query heads share a single KV head (H_KV = 1).
cards.buy: Maximum KV reduction vs full MHA — cache slope drops sharply.
cards.give_up: Quality can drop vs MHA/GQA if sharing is too aggressive; does not remove T² prefill compute.
cards.when: Latency-sensitive decoding at large batch where KV RAM dominates.

cards.title: Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)
cards.problem: MQA saves memory but can hurt quality; MHA is accurate but expensive to cache.
cards.mechanism: Share KV heads among groups of query heads: 1 < H_KV < H_Q.
cards.buy: Practical middle ground — Llama/Mistral-class default; KVReduction = H_Q / H_KV.
cards.give_up: Still linear KV growth with T; prefill compute bill largely unchanged.
cards.when: Production open models balancing quality and multi-user KV footprint.

source.label: Ainslie et al. — GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Attention

cards.title: Sliding-window (local) attention
cards.problem: Global T² attention is unaffordable at very long sequences.
cards.mechanism: Each token attends only within a fixed local window of past positions.
cards.buy: Compute and memory per layer scale ≈ T×W instead of T² for window W.
cards.give_up: Tokens outside the window are invisible unless another layer or mechanism bridges distance.
cards.when: Very long streams where local context dominates (some Mistral/Longformer-style stacks).
cards.sec_note: §7 sparse/window family; Longformer; no own h1

cards.title: Attention sinks
cards.problem: Streaming and windowed models can destabilize when no token accumulates “rest” mass in softmax.
cards.mechanism: Reserve early tokens (often BOS) as sinks that absorb attention mass during long runs.
cards.give_up: Heuristic — sinks consume capacity; not a substitute for true long-range retrieval.
cards.when: Streaming LLM serving with fixed windows where softmax drift was observed.

source.label: Xiao et al. — Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks

cards.title: NTK-aware RoPE scaling
cards.problem: RoPE bands wrap at lengths beyond training; positions alias and quality collapses.
cards.mechanism: Rescale rotary base / frequencies so effective wavelengths fit longer serve context (NTK-inspired).
cards.buy: Cheaper than full retrain for moderate length stretch on RoPE models.
cards.give_up: Extension ceiling; not identical to native long-context training.
cards.when: Road 1 stretch: serve modestly beyond train length on existing RoPE checkpoints.
cards.sec_note: Web.htm §15 long-context system mentions; no own h1

cards.title: YaRN (Yet another RoPE extensioN)
cards.problem: Naive NTK scaling alone may blur high-frequency bands needed for fine local structure.
cards.mechanism: Blend/interpolate RoPE frequencies during extension so local and global bands behave at long T.
cards.buy: Reported strong stretch factors (e.g. Qwen-class long context) without full retrain.
cards.give_up: Hyperparameters and model-specific tuning; still an extrapolation hack vs native long train.
cards.when: Road 1 when you need larger stretch than bare NTK on open RoPE models.

source.label: Peng et al. — YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension

cards.title: Linear attention (softmax off, state S)
cards.problem: Exact attention requires visiting all past keys — T² compute and growing KV.
cards.mechanism: Remove softmax; fold history into fixed-size state S: S ← S + v kᵀ, read y = S q.
cards.buy: Fixed memory state; sub-quadratic recurrence on compatible formulations.
cards.give_up: Not equivalent to softmax attention; different expressivity and training recipe.
cards.when: When you accept softmax-off training and need bounded state instead of full KV.

source.label: Katharopoulos et al. — Transformers are RNNs (linear attention)

cards.title: Delta rule write
cards.problem: Pure additive state S ← S + v kᵀ cannot cleanly overwrite stale memory for a repeated key.
cards.mechanism: Read v̂ = S k, write only correction Δ = v − v̂; exact overwrite needs ||k||₂ = 1.
cards.buy: Targeted memory updates instead of blind accumulation.
cards.give_up: Requires normalized keys or stated convention; more fragile than softmax retrieval.
cards.when: DeltaNet-style layers where keys should update slots in place.

source.label: Yang et al. — Parallelizing Linear Transformers with the Delta Rule

cards.title: Gated DeltaNet
cards.problem: Un gated delta writes can be too aggressive or too weak depending on context gate.
cards.mechanism: Gate the delta write so the model learns when to trust state updates vs leave history.
cards.buy: Selective writes — better control than always-on delta.
cards.give_up: Extra parameters and training complexity; must tune gate schedule with sparse/linear mix.
cards.when: Hybrid stacks (DDDG-style) mixing delta state layers with gated sparse layers.

source.label: Yang et al. — Gated Delta Networks

cards.sec_note: After delta in transcript; V4 schedule §13 also references; no own h1

cards.title: Sparse / top-k attention
cards.problem: Even with GQA, prefill still compares each query to many keys — T² in dense form.
cards.mechanism: Keep softmax but only on top-k past keys per query; budget ≈ T·k.
cards.buy: Cuts comparisons while keeping softmax semantics on survivors.
cards.give_up: Missed keys → wrong answers; k becomes a hard recall–cost knob.
cards.when: Long context where most mass is local or indexer picks likely keys.

source.label: Roy et al. — Routing Transformer (content-based sparse / k-means routing)

cards.title: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA)
cards.problem: KV still stores full head dimensions per token even after GQA.
cards.mechanism: Compress KV into a lower-dimensional latent before cache; expand on read.
cards.buy: Further KV byte reduction on top of head sharing.
cards.give_up: Compression loss; implementation and kernel coupling; Road-2 style complexity.
cards.when: DeepSeek-class serving where cache bytes dominate at long T.
cards.sec_note: Web.htm §12 sequence compression / DeepSeek MLA family

cards.title: DeepSeek compressed sparse attention
cards.problem: Sparse top-k alone still stores full-length KV; indexer + blocks must co-design.
cards.mechanism: Block summaries plus sparse reads — compression (T→T/m) combined with selective attention.
cards.buy: Attacks both compute and memory bills aggressively.
cards.give_up: Indexer errors are catastrophic; training and infra heavier than dense GQA.
cards.when: Road 2 native long-context training with compression-first architecture.

cards.title: DroPE (extension factor)
cards.problem: Training at full 256K is prohibitively expensive; RoPE alone breaks at serve length.
cards.mechanism: Train short, serve long: ExtensionFactor = serve_len / train_len with positional recalibration (V4 story 8K→256K = 32×).
cards.buy: Affordable train bill; reported large context on Road 1.
cards.give_up: Extension ceiling vs native long train; algorithm details must match checkpoint recipe.
cards.when: Road 1 stretch when product needs 256K serve with 8K-class train budget.

source.label: YaRN paper — V4 DroPE extension-factor story (not Sakana drop-PE)
